title: Mermaid Madness
build: Kurt crack, MERMAID MADNESS from C64.com D64

tools.emulator: VICE v3.14.0 macOS arm64 headless, dummy audio

exclude: Physical RAM outside VIC bank zero. The second unpacker writes both mirrored copies before $4000. Play leaves I/O and KERNAL visible and the alternate release does not share these bytes.
Kurt packing residue beneath KERNAL. Startup stores hit here with $01 = $34, and game entry keeps KERNAL visible.
Generated screen bytes and VIC sprite pointers. The hand-over screen is spaces, and the game clears and rebuilds the screen from $418E, $450F and the HUD routines.
6510 port, KERNAL workspace and zero-page runtime state. Game variables and pointers are initialized or overwritten by their respective routines.
KERNAL workspace and RAM vectors set at start-up. The remaining setup bytes are outside the game engine called at $4000.
Runtime actor, object, gauge, movement and redraw state. $407D clears its working fields and initializes the attempt. $4450 is the separately recorded retained high-score field.
Music sequencer counters and work bytes written by $9024, $90DE and $91C5.
Mutable SID driver state for effect pitches, counters and current track. It is updated by SID routines as they run.

Loaded bytes beyond the eight metatile attribute pages. The byte-indexed attributes end at $87FF and the engine’s indirect graphics sources address the bitmap, item texts, paths and sprite banks elsewhere. A redraw watch observed 1,024 attribute reads and zero reads in this range.
Bytes after the SID driver state, including a fragment with KERNAL I/O calls. The game’s indexed SID reads here are bounded to X=0 or 2 for the pitch pair and X=0–3 for effect envelopes.

Variant-specific Kurt loader code and data. Startup stores hit $CC80 before $4000 in the second depack. No engine call or decoded data reference reaches this region, and the Remember entry uses different bytes.
